title: High-Performance Tall Buildings: An Overview of  Recent Developments
content: The evolution of tall buildings has been shaped by distinct architectural styles, beginning around 1875 and progressing through various stylistic architectural movements. These changes were driven by advancements in structural engineering and subsequent digital design technologies, leading to greater experimentation with form and function. In particular, the early 21st century saw a significant shift toward a new breed of tall buildings, a suitable architectural vocabulary for which is “high-performance” tall buildings, in which sustainability with a focus on energy efficiency is joined with other active and passive functional systems. High performance is thus a concept that goes beyond sustainability. This paper presents an overview of high-performance tall buildings by exploring the key technologies, materials, innovations, safety, durability, interior environment, and more. It highlights the importance of optimizing and combining innovative and durable functionality of building systems, minimum resource consumption, occupant health and comfort, improved productivity, and continuous performance monitoring to ensure long-term viability. Furthermore, the paper underlines high-performance buildings' environmental and economic benefits, offering strategies for enhancing future design targets to create more appropriate and livable urban landscapes.
